markdown_report:
Choose a **serving-aligned candidate difficulty audit** before changing BERT4Rec’s training objective. At 0% progress, this offers a small, interpretable experiment without additional fitted predictors.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, earlier runs passed serving checks, while another adapter lacked routing and replay inputs. Diagnostic availability must therefore be established for the current checkpoint rather than inherited from previous reports. Second, recent-item deletion reduced target scores across categories, but diagnostic hit-rate intervals included zero. Sensitivity alone does not establish useful temporal prediction. Third, feedback distinguishes broad relevance from immediate choice and unidentified items. These observations motivate diagnosis but provide neither negative relevance labels nor evidence of compatibility or mood.

Three literature insights organize the next steps. Sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons, motivating comparisons across candidate constructions [1]. Frequency-stratified findings motivate reporting head/tail differences, without assuming their causes transfer to BERT4Rec [2]. BERT4Rec’s masked objective requires target removal from bidirectional input, so every next-item audit must use a prefix followed by MASK [3].

The conceptual framework connects three directions:

| Direction | Controlled comparison | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Execution validity | Current versus exported checkpoint scores | Untested production paths |
| Candidate difficulty | Uniform, frequency-matched, lexical candidates | Candidates are not verified dislikes |
| Temporal specificity | Fixed-candidate history perturbations | Sensitivity is not usefulness |

Three atomic ideas are worth considering. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate difficulty audit [1,2] | 4/7/3 | Simple synthesis; reusable diagnosis; existing scorer suffices | Established methods; diagnostic value may not yield gains; eligibility bookkeeping remains |
| Anchored older-history shuffle [3] | 3/5/3 | Isolates an order hypothesis; supports temporal studies; simple perturbation | Familiar intervention; weak effects may be inconclusive; position controls need care |
| Evidence-linked feedback labels | 3/6/4 | Separates abstention from rejection; improves future annotations; no model change | Conventional taxonomy; twenty users limit inference; reliable coding requires review |

For the selected audit, use fixed public training prefixes with unseen next-item targets. Construct three equal-sized sets containing the target and 99 unique eligible candidates: uniform, target-frequency-band matched, and lexical title/description neighbors. Use training-only frequencies and locally computed TF-IDF; lexical similarity selects diagnostic candidates and never contributes prediction scores. Repeat three seeded draws, preserve common users, and report shortages explicitly.

Score all sets with the same appended-MASK BERT4Rec. Report paired target ranks, target-minus-tenth-negative margins, hit flips, counts, and user-clustered descriptive intervals by category and training-frequency band. Preserve diagnostic interfaces, restore modes/RNG state, and cap audit compute beforehand. Train and deploy exactly one model per category; retain all routing, seeds, training limits, and predictor consistency. Select solely through unchanged host macro validation HR@10. No improvement is established yet.

[1] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/
[2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276
[3] https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690

idea.description: Add a small serving-aligned candidate difficulty audit to the corrected BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter. Compare the same public training-prefix targets under uniform, training-frequency-matched, and lexical-neighbor candidate sets, scoring every item exclusively with the category’s single trained BERT4Rec.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics and qualitative feedback do not establish a training repair. Candidate construction can affect sampled rankings, so measuring how this particular checkpoint behaves under controlled candidate difficulty can distinguish easy sampled separation from more specific discrimination without asserting semantic relevance or changing the host evaluator.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep the corrected baseline training and scoring architecture unchanged for this experiment. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch, and every ModelView interface. Pass actual category identity from the training loop. Capture at most ten independently cloned batches already consumed by training for existing sampler/margin probes; do not advance the live training iterator to populate replay. Run probes independently and retain completed results with definitions, counts, statuses, and specific failure reasons. Missing replay blocks only dependent probes.

Before interpreting scoring results, verify the current serialized category checkpoint against view.model and compare internal/exported appended-MASK scores on short, full-length, truncated, and batched histories. A previous run’s parity result is insufficient. Preserve final-nonpadding readout using the maximum valid position index, never nonpadding-count minus one. For the canonical left-padded appended-MASK input this is maxlen-1. Preserve PAD=0 and reserved MASK=itemnum+1; neither is a candidate. Keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb, and predict_score(features, items) compatible.

Select up to 32 eligible users/category with a dedicated seed-42 generator, before examining scores, and one uniformly selected eligible endpoint/user. Require at least four preceding interactions and a target absent from the complete preceding prefix. Construct the input solely from that prefix’s final maxlen-1 items plus MASK; later interactions never enter input or candidate eligibility. Count exclusions. Compute item frequencies from public training histories only. Freeze frequency bands [1,4), [4,16), [16,64), [64,256), [256,infinity), with a separate zero-frequency band if needed.

For each endpoint build three candidate regimes, each with one target and 99 unique real items excluding the complete prefix and target. Uniform candidates come from the full eligible catalog. Frequency-matched candidates come from the target’s frozen frequency band; fewer than 99 makes that regime unavailable for the endpoint, without silent relaxation. Lexical candidates come from the top 500 eligible title/description neighbors, ordered by locally fitted TF-IDF cosine then item ID, followed by uniform selection of 99 from that pool. Missing target text, fewer than 99 positive-similarity neighbors, or inadequate pools yield explicit unavailability. Fit TF-IDF solely on supplied public catalog text, once per category, with a fixed feature cap. Report text coverage. Similarity is neither compatibility nor verified substitutability.

Use three predefined candidate draws and the same checkpoint throughout. Score candidates in chunks if needed. Rank with descending neural score then ascending item ID for diagnostic reproducibility; leave host tie handling unchanged. Report raw target ranks, target-minus-tenth-negative margins, diagnostic hit@10, and pairwise hit flips across regimes. Restrict paired comparisons to endpoints available in both regimes and report their denominator. Report per-regime availability separately to expose selection differences. Stratify descriptively by training-frequency band and visible-history length; do not tune band boundaries after seeing outcomes. Bootstrap users with their repeated draws kept together; intervals condition on checkpoint, selected users, and construction protocol.

Predeclare a 15-second soft GPU audit cap/category and record CPU preparation, synchronized GPU execution time, completed users/draws, failures, and cap overruns. Partial results remain labeled partial. Use evaluation mode and no gradients; restore individual module modes and controlled RNG states in finally blocks. Audit mutable forward behavior before using the live model; a disposable copy of the same checkpoint may be used solely for diagnostics, without fitting or deployment. Do not impose unrelated unavailable-data gates on valid probes.

Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl; preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches/epoch, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five designated real training users/category. Each category trains and loads exactly one model/checkpoint. No score fusion, separately fitted relevance scorer, checkpoint averaging, pretrained weights, hidden test access, or cross-trial checkpoint reuse. Keep checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor writer synchronized. Only the unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10 determines selection; these training-prefix measurements do not estimate full-catalog performance or prove validation improvement.

originality.positive: Combines candidate-difficulty controls with serving-aligned BERT4Rec diagnostics and explicit availability accounting.
originality.negative: Candidate sampling, frequency stratification, and lexical neighborhoods are established techniques; this is a task-specific diagnostic synthesis.

future_potential.positive: Can support focused later hypotheses about sampling and discrimination while providing a reusable audit across all four categories.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic differences may not identify an effective training change or predict gains under the pinned host evaluation.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the trained model and existing scoring interfaces without architecture changes or additional training.
code_difficulty.negative: Current-checkpoint parity, sparse lexical retrieval, candidate shortages, and paired availability require careful integration.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
Motivates examining sensitivity to candidate construction.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied BERT4Rec has a candidate-discrimination defect.
Does not justify altering the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: Prakash et al., sequential recommendation study supplied in search results
contributions: The supplied summary reports that aggregate metrics conceal item-frequency differences.
limitations: Reported sampling tradeoffs do not establish the cause of this checkpoint’s behavior.
Frequency strata do not provide semantic relevance or dislike labels.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Provides the masked-target foundation for appended-MASK next-item scoring.
limitations: The original objective does not guarantee compatibility reasoning or immediate-choice relevance.
Correct implementation and current exported-serving parity still require direct verification.
